This is a READ-ONLY audit of the git repo at /mnt/c/Projects/biotech_screener/biotech-screener/ (branch main). DO NOT edit, create, or delete any files. DO NOT run git add/commit/push or any command that mutates the working tree. Only use Read, Grep, Glob, and read-only Bash (cat/grep/find/git log/git show/git status/git diff are fine; no mutating git commands).

Background: In this biotech investing model, options-derived data (implied vol, straddle prices, priced moves, etc.) are policy-closed for use in alpha/selector/ranker decisions — 37 options-based signals were tested previously and rejected for predictive use. Per current policy, options data is approved ONLY as overlay/diagnostic infrastructure: priced-move integrity checks, event-vol diagnostics, liquidity confidence scoring, and staleness/null handling — NOT as inputs to scoring, ranking, selection, or sizing decisions.

Your job is to verify whether this policy is actually respected in the codebase, and to survey the existing Spec 059 diagnostic coverage. Do all 6 tasks below and report back with file:line citations and short code quotes as evidence.

TASK 1: Find `event_ev/surface_diagnostics.py` and `event_ev/branch_sensitivity.py`. If not at that exact path, search with `find . -iname "surface_diagnostics.py" -o -iname "branch_sensitivity.py"`. Read both files fully. Report what fields/metrics each computes, with file:line citations. Specifically determine and report whether they compute or approximate: forward vol, skew, term structure, and any "liquidity confidence" style score.

TASK 2: Find any existing options coverage reports or scripts. Search with `grep -rl "options.*coverage\|coverage.*options" --include=*.py .` and also check for an `artifacts/` or `reports/` directory containing existing options coverage outputs (e.g. find artifacts/ -iname "*options*"). Report what you find.

TASK 3: Find production snapshot export logic that touches options fields. Search for where rankings.csv or snapshot export code references options-related field names: straddle_price, priced_move_pct, implied_vol, options_, event_ev, liquidity_confidence, liquidity_rating. Use grep across the repo (exclude .git, node_modules, venv if present). Give file:line citations for each reference found in export/snapshot code.

TASK 4: Find existing tests for options / event_ev / expectation fields. Run `find . -iname "*test*options*" -o -iname "*test*event_ev*"`, and also grep test directories for "straddle_price\|priced_move_pct\|options_diagnostics". List test files found and briefly summarize (skim level, not exhaustive) what each covers.

TASK 5 (CRITICAL — leakage trace): Find selector/ranker/final_score/sizing/portfolio construction code — look for files named like `selector.py`, `ranker.py`, `final_score.py`, `sizing.py`, `portfolio.py`, likely under a `core/`, `model/`, or `pipeline/` directory (use find/glob to locate them first). For EACH such file, grep for these field names: `straddle_price`, `priced_move_pct`, `implied_vol`, `options_diagnostics`, `event_ev`, `surface_diagnostics`, `branch_sensitivity`, `liquidity_rating`, `liquidity_confidence`. For every hit, show file:line plus a few lines of surrounding context, and assess: is this field actually READ and USED in a score/weight/selection/sizing decision (i.e. does it affect a numeric score, a filter/threshold, or inclusion/exclusion logic), or is it merely passed through / logged / written to an output column without affecting decisions?

TASK 6 (lineage trace): Determine whether outputs of surface_diagnostics.py / branch_sensitivity.py / any options_diagnostics module get written to a file, dataframe column, or return value that downstream selector/ranker code then reads. Concretely: (a) find where these modules' outputs are written (return value consumed by caller, file write, csv column name), (b) then grep the rest of the pipeline for those same field/column names being read OUTSIDE the diagnostic modules themselves, particularly in any file from Task 5. Trace the actual call chain / data flow as concretely as you can (who calls surface_diagnostics/branch_sensitivity, what does the caller do with the return value, does that flow into selector/ranker inputs).

Report back in plain text, organized strictly by task number (1-6), with file:line citations and short code quotes as evidence for every claim. At the very TOP of your report, before task 1, include a clearly marked section titled "LEAKAGE FLAG" — if you find ANY case where an options-derived field is read and actually used in a score/weight/selection/sizing/inclusion decision in selector/ranker/final_score/sizing/portfolio code, state this prominently with file:line. If you find NO such leakage (i.e. all options fields in decision-logic files are shadow-only/passthrough/logged), state that clearly too. Be precise and conservative — don't claim leakage unless you can show the field's value actually flows into a computation that affects score/rank/selection/size, not just that the field name appears nearby (e.g. in a comment, docstring, or an unrelated function).

This is pure research/reporting — do not write any files, do not propose code changes, just report findings in your final message text.

This is a READ-ONLY audit of the git repo at /mnt/c/Projects/biotech_screener/biotech-screener/ (branch main). DO NOT edit, create, or delete any files. DO NOT run git add/commit/push or any command that mutates the working tree. Only use Read, Grep, Glob, and read-only Bash (cat/grep/find/git log/git show/git status/git diff are fine; no mutating git commands).

Background: In this biotech investing model, options-derived data (implied vol, straddle prices, priced moves, etc.) are policy-closed for use in alpha/selector/ranker decisions — 37 options-based signals were tested previously and rejected for predictive use. Per current policy, options data is approved ONLY as overlay/diagnostic infrastructure: priced-move integrity checks, event-vol diagnostics, liquidity confidence scoring, and staleness/null handling — NOT as inputs to scoring, ranking, selection, or sizing decisions.

Your job is to verify whether this policy is actually respected in the codebase, and to survey the existing Spec 059 diagnostic coverage. Do all 6 tasks below and report back with file:line citations and short code quotes as evidence.

TASK 1: Find `event_ev/surface_diagnostics.py` and `event_ev/branch_sensitivity.py`. If not at that exact path, search with `find . -iname "surface_diagnostics.py" -o -iname "branch_sensitivity.py"`. Read both files fully. Report what fields/metrics each computes, with file:line citations. Specifically determine and report whether they compute or approximate: forward vol, skew, term structure, and any "liquidity confidence" style score.

TASK 2: Find any existing options coverage reports or scripts. Search with `grep -rl "options.*coverage\|coverage.*options" --include=*.py .` and also check for an `artifacts/` or `reports/` directory containing existing options coverage outputs (e.g. find artifacts/ -iname "*options*"). Report what you find.

TASK 3: Find production snapshot export logic that touches options fields. Search for where rankings.csv or snapshot export code references options-related field names: straddle_price, priced_move_pct, implied_vol, options_, event_ev, liquidity_confidence, liquidity_rating. Use grep across the repo (exclude .git, node_modules, venv if present). Give file:line citations for each reference found in export/snapshot code.

TASK 4: Find existing tests for options / event_ev / expectation fields. Run `find . -iname "*test*options*" -o -iname "*test*event_ev*"`, and also grep test directories for "straddle_price\|priced_move_pct\|options_diagnostics". List test files found and briefly summarize (skim level, not exhaustive) what each covers.

TASK 5 (CRITICAL — leakage trace): Find selector/ranker/final_score/sizing/portfolio construction code — look for files named like `selector.py`, `ranker.py`, `final_score.py`, `sizing.py`, `portfolio.py`, likely under a `core/`, `model/`, or `pipeline/` directory (use find/glob to locate them first). For EACH such file, grep for these field names: `straddle_price`, `priced_move_pct`, `implied_vol`, `options_diagnostics`, `event_ev`, `surface_diagnostics`, `branch_sensitivity`, `liquidity_rating`, `liquidity_confidence`. For every hit, show file:line plus a few lines of surrounding context, and assess: is this field actually READ and USED in a score/weight/selection/sizing decision (i.e. does it affect a numeric score, a filter/threshold, or inclusion/exclusion logic), or is it merely passed through / logged / written to an output column without affecting decisions?

TASK 6 (lineage trace): Determine whether outputs of surface_diagnostics.py / branch_sensitivity.py / any options_diagnostics module get written to a file, dataframe column, or return value that downstream selector/ranker code then reads. Concretely: (a) find where these modules' outputs are written (return value consumed by caller, file write, csv column name), (b) then grep the rest of the pipeline for those same field/column names being read OUTSIDE the diagnostic modules themselves, particularly in any file from Task 5. Trace the actual call chain / data flow as concretely as you can (who calls surface_diagnostics/branch_sensitivity, what does the caller do with the return value, does that flow into selector/ranker inputs).

Report back in plain text, organized strictly by task number (1-6), with file:line citations and short code quotes as evidence for every claim. At the very TOP of your report, before task 1, include a clearly marked section titled "LEAKAGE FLAG" — if you find ANY case where an options-derived field is read and actually used in a score/weight/selection/sizing/inclusion decision in selector/ranker/final_score/sizing/portfolio code, state this prominently with file:line. If you find NO such leakage (i.e. all options fields in decision-logic files are shadow-only/passthrough/logged), state that clearly too. Be precise and conservative — don't claim leakage unless you can show the field's value actually flows into a computation that affects score/rank/selection/size, not just that the field name appears nearby (e.g. in a comment, docstring, or an unrelated function).

This is pure research/reporting — do not write any files, do not propose code changes, just report findings in your final message text.

<result>The audit is complete. Here's the report:

## LEAKAGE FLAG

**NO LEAKAGE FOUND.** None of the options-derived field names (`straddle_price`, `priced_move_pct`, `implied_vol`, `options_diagnostics`, `event_ev`, `surface_diagnostics`, `branch_sensitivity`, `liquidity_rating`, `liquidity_confidence`) appear anywhere in `ranker_engine.py`, `ranker_v2_pairwise.py`, `selector_engine.py`, `portfolio_risk_layer.py`, `portfolio_vol_corr_layer.py`, or `event_ev/portfolio_sizing.py`. The only production file touching these fields is `run_screen.py`, and concrete line-order evidence shows selector scoring (line 5806) and ranker scoring (line 5844) both execute **before** `priced_move_pct`/`straddle_price` are even populated (line 6848, with an explicit code comment warning this ordering was the source of a past P0 bug). Downstream uses of these fields write only to sidecar JSON/CSV artifacts and a dashboard display endpoint — never back into score/rank/weight.

## Task 1 — surface_diagnostics.py / branch_sensitivity.py
Both at `event_ev/`, both carry explicit "OVERLAY-ONLY, no selector/ranker impact" docstrings.
- **surface_diagnostics.py**: `classify_term_structure()` (term-structure shape via front/back IV ratio), `detect_surface_anomalies()` (z-score anomaly detection), `compare_to_history()` (percentile vs own history), `compute_belief_intensity_modifier()` (confidence-band modifier, explicitly NOT a feature weight per in-code comment).
- **branch_sensitivity.py**: Black-Scholes branch P&L via crush-ratio approximation, breakeven-straddle diagnostic.
- Forward vol: approximated via crush ratio, not modeled directly. Skew: not computed in these two files (exists elsewhere as `opt_rr_25d`). Term structure: yes. Liquidity confidence score: no — only a binary/categorical hard-gate (`liquid`/`thin`/`absent`), not a continuous score.

## Task 2 — Existing coverage reports
Dedicated tool `scripts/diagnostics/options_coverage_audit.py`; artifacts under `artifacts/diagnostics/options_coverage_audit_*.json` and `artifacts/options_enrichment/{dates}/` (latest 2026-06-30 report explicitly tagged `NO_MODEL_CHANGE/NO_RANKER_CHANGE/NO_SELECTOR_CHANGE/NO_SIZING_CHANGE`).

## Task 3 — Snapshot export references
All hits in `run_screen.py` are CSV-column population or sidecar-file writes (e.g. lines 4432-4436, 6380-6445, 7135/7182, 8012, 8682) — not score computations.

## Task 4 — Test coverage
24 test files found, including direct unit tests `tests/test_surface_diagnostics.py` (19 tests) and `tests/test_branch_sensitivity.py` (15 tests), plus broader options-pipeline tests (`test_event_ev_engine.py`, `test_options_diagnostics.py`, etc.).

## Task 5 — Leakage trace in decision files
Zero hits for any of the 9 options field names in all 7 selector/ranker/sizing/portfolio files checked. Nothing to assess as passthrough vs. used — the fields are simply absent from these files entirely.

## Task 6 — Lineage trace
`surface_anomalies.json` (from `detect_surface_anomalies`) is read only by `dashboard/app.py`'s display endpoints — never by any selector/ranker/sizing file. `EventEV.branch_sensitivity` stays internal to the `event_ev` object model. The strongest evidence is the execution order in `run_screen.py`: selector/ranker scoring happens at lines 5806/5844, while options fields like `priced_move_pct`/`straddle_price` aren't populated until lines 6360-6848 — chronologically after scoring is already complete, with no subsequent re-computation of score/rank/weight using those fields.

**Conclusion**: Spec 059 and the broader options/event_ev overlay are architecturally and temporally isolated from the selector/ranker/sizing/portfolio decision path. Policy appears respected on `main` as of 2026-06-30.</result>

## Audit complete — no policy violation found

**LEAKAGE FLAG: NONE.** Options-derived fields are not read or used in any selector/ranker/sizing/portfolio decision logic on `main` as of 2026-06-30. The policy (options data = overlay/diagnostic only, never a scoring/ranking/selection/sizing input) is respected.

**Key evidence:**
- None of `straddle_price`, `priced_move_pct`, `implied_vol`, `options_diagnostics`, `event_ev`, `surface_diagnostics`, `branch_sensitivity`, `liquidity_rating`, `liquidity_confidence` appear anywhere in `ranker_engine.py`, `ranker_v2_pairwise.py`, `selector_engine.py`, `portfolio_risk_layer.py`, `portfolio_vol_corr_layer.py`, or `event_ev/portfolio_sizing.py`.
- The one production file that does touch these fields, `run_screen.py`, shows a clean temporal separation: selector scoring runs at line 5806 and ranker scoring at line 5844 — **before** `priced_move_pct`/`straddle_price` are even populated (line 6848). A code comment there explicitly flags this ordering as the fix for a prior P0 bug where options data leaked into scoring.
- Downstream, options outputs only ever land in sidecar JSON/CSV artifacts or a dashboard display endpoint (`dashboard/app.py`) — never back into score/rank/weight computation.

**Task summaries:**
1. **`event_ev/surface_diagnostics.py`** computes term-structure classification, surface anomaly z-scores, historical percentile comparison, and a "belief intensity modifier" explicitly documented as non-feature-weight. **`event_ev/branch_sensitivity.py`** computes Black-Scholes branch P&L via crush-ratio approximation and a breakeven-straddle diagnostic. Forward vol is approximated only via crush ratio; skew is not computed in these two files (lives elsewhere as `opt_rr_25d`); term structure is computed; "liquidity confidence" exists only as a categorical hard-gate (liquid/thin/absent), not a continuous score. Both files carry explicit "OVERLAY-ONLY, no selector/ranker impact" docstrings.
2. Dedicated `scripts/diagnostics/options_coverage_audit.py` tool with output artifacts under `artifacts/diagnostics/options_coverage_audit_*.json` and `artifacts/options_enrichment/`; the latest (2026-06-30) report is explicitly tagged `NO_MODEL_CHANGE/NO_RANKER_CHANGE/NO_SELECTOR_CHANGE/NO_SIZING_CHANGE`.
3. All options-field references in export/snapshot code are CSV-column writes or sidecar-file writes in `run_screen.py` (e.g. lines 4432-4436, 6380-6445, 7135/7182, 8012, 8682) — not score computations.
4. 24 related test files, including direct unit tests `tests/test_surface_diagnostics.py` (19 tests) and `tests/test_branch_sensitivity.py` (15 tests), plus broader pipeline tests (`test_event_ev_engine.py`, `test_options_diagnostics.py`).
5. Zero hits for any of the 9 options field names across all 7 selector/ranker/sizing/portfolio files — nothing to flag as passthrough vs. used because the fields don't appear there at all.
6. `surface_anomalies.json` output is consumed only by the dashboard display layer, never by selector/ranker/sizing. `branch_sensitivity` output stays internal to the `event_ev` object model. The decisive trace is the line-order proof in `run_screen.py`: scoring completes before options fields are even populated, so no re-computation downstream could incorporate them.

This matches and reinforces the existing memory note on Spec 059-adjacent governance — happy to write this up as a memory file if you want it tracked, but per instructions I haven't created or modified anything.
